Quick triage notes (initial):
- Observed mass KV cache evictions in the serving tier starting 07:46, exact alignment with model rollout kickoff. Eviction count ~10x baseline.
- Cause hypothesis: rollout introduced a minor protobuf schema tweak in model manifest that changed the hashed prefix for dynamic prompts. Result: cache keys no longer matched and we experienced a cold-cache storm across many workers.
- Secondary: eviction storm caused increased memory pressure -> worker GC + transient 503s while autoscaler tried to rebalance.

Immediate mitigation plan (recommended):
1) Pause active rollout and pin traffic to pre-v12 model variants for impacted regions (us-west) — ETA 10 mins.
2) Initiate controlled worker restarts with increased local cache TTL to allow soft-warm-up (no full wipes) — ETA 20-30 mins after pause.
3) Apply a rollback of the manifest change in the rollout repo and re-run warm-start for the cohort — ETA 45-60 mins for full stabilization.

Attachments: kv-eviction-runbook.md (snippet of steps we followed). I will run the pause now and post back with progress.

— Soojin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

We've paused the rollout for us-west and started a targeted rollback of the manifest change. Expected impact timeline: we should see p95 and 503s begin to normalize within 30–45 minutes.

Planned next steps (what we're doing right now):
- Pause rollout for us-west (done).
- Controlled worker restarts with elevated local cache TTL to avoid full cold-warm (in progress).

We will notify you the moment we see stability. Apologies for the disruption — we understand checkout latency is critical for ParcelPatch. If you want a technical postmortem and a remediation plan, we will share one within 48 hours.
